 3m ago 07.27 EST Here are more of Xi’s speech (as per Xinhua):
 double quotation mark At tomorrow’s Leaders’ Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual openness, explore pathways for innovation-driven growth, broaden opportunities for pragmatic cooperation in various fields, and promote the implementation of more outcomes. I look forward to discussing the grand plan for Asia-Pacific cooperation and jointly advancing the cause of Asia-Pacific development with you all.
 Now, I propose that we raise a glass together.
 For the common prosperity of the Asia-Pacific region,
 For the success of this informal leaders’ meeting,
 For the health of all guests and their families,
 Cheers!
 View image in fullscreen Xi Jinping raises a toast at the Apec welcome banquet. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/Pool Reuters/AP Share Updated at  07.27 EST 13m ago 07.17 EST Xi hails Shenzhen's transformation in Apec banquet speech
 China’s state news agency Xinhua has published the text of Xi Jinping’s welcome speech at tonight’s Apec banquet in Shenzhen.
 In his remarks, Xi praised the city’s transformation into an international economic and innovation hub, describing it as a symbol of China’s development.
 Here are a few passages from his address:
 double quotation mark This evening, the shores of the South China Sea are aglow with lights, and autumn is in full swing here in Shenzhen, the City of the Phoenix. As the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting is about to commence, I would like, on behalf of the Chinese Government and the Chinese people, to extend a warm welcome to all our distinguished guests.
 I have often said that to see a thousand years of China, one should visit Xi’an; to see five hundred years of China, one should visit Beijing; and to see a hundred years of China, one should visit Shanghai. Today, I would like to say to you all: to see fifty years of China, come to Shenzhen.
 Shenzhen is a place with a rich history. In 1978, when I first came to Shenzhen, it was still a small fishing village. More than 40 years have passed in the blink of an eye, and now it is filled with high-rise buildings and bustling traffic. The changes are truly remarkable.”
 View image in fullscreen Chinese president Xi Jinping speaks at a welcome banquet for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/AFP/Getty Images Share 51m ago 06.39 EST Trump and Putin shake hands ahead of Apec welcome banquet
 US president Donald Trump shakes hands with Russian president Vladimir Putin , as China’s Xi Jinping looks on, ahead of the welcome banquet at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China:
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Iori Sagisawa/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  06.54 EST 1h ago 06.33 EST Donald Trump has arrived at the welcome banquet with Xi Jinping:
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/Reuters Share 1h ago 06.31 EST The newswires are carrying pictures of world leaders arriving for the welcome banquet at the Apec summit, including Russia’s Vladimir Putin:
 View image in fullscreen Vladimir Putin arrives at the welcome banquet for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China on Wednesday. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP View image in fullscreen Attendees gather for the banquet hosted by Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese arrives at the banquet. Photograph: Lukas Coch/AAP Share 1h ago 06.04 EST Putin and Trump could meet informally during Apec summit, Russia state media reports
 Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump could have several opportunities to speak during the Apec summit in China, according to Russia’s state news agency, Tass.
 Citing Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov , Tass reported that the two leaders could exchange words informally at various points during the summit.
 They will communicate “on their feet, on the steps, in chairs”, Ushakov reportedly said, suggesting their interactions need not be limited to a formal sit-down meeting.
 Share Updated at  06.08 EST 2h ago 05.38 EST Xi says he hopes to build 'stable' China-US ties with Trump - state media
 Xi Jinping told Donald Trump he hoped their talks would help advance a “constructive, strategic and stable relationship” between China and the US, based on “respect, fairness and reciprocity” , according to China’s state news agency Xinhua .
 Xi also recalled Trump’s personal welcome at the airport during his visit to the US in September, saying China’s own welcome for the US president reflected its tradition of reciprocity.
 Xinhua reported the following remarks by the Chinese president:
 double quotation mark When I visited the United States in September this year, president Trump and his wife made a special trip to the airport to welcome me, and a grand welcoming ceremony was held.
 China is a nation of courtesy, with a tradition of reciprocity. I welcome you back to China and look forward to exchanging in-depth views with you on major issues concerning China–US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation and the global landscape, so as to advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship between China and the US based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.”
 View image in fullscreen Donald Trump is welcomed by Xi Jinping at Shenzhen Bao'an airport on Wednesday. Photograph: Win McNamee/Getty Images Share 3h ago 04.58 EST Xi hails ‘unshaken’ China-Russia ties after talks with Putin
 Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen 
 Chinese state media have released a readout of Xi Jinping’s earlier meeting with Vladimir Putin .
 In it, Xi is quoted as saying China-Russia relations are “unshaken by storms and steady as a mountain” , and have set “an example of a new type of major-country relationship characterised by equality, mutual respect, trustworthiness, and win-win co-operation”.
 Xi also urged closer political and military ties between the two countries.
 He said “the two sides should leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries’ governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties, ensuring that the consensus reached by the two countries’ heads of state is effectively implemented”, according to the readout.
 View image in fullscreen Russian president Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping hold talks in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. Photograph: Kremlin Press Service/Anadolu/Getty Images Share Updated at  05.26 EST 3h ago 04.39 EST In a notable gesture, Xi personally greeted Trump on the airport tarmac in Shenzhen , reciprocating the welcome the US president extended to the Chinese leader during his visit to the US in September.
 View image in fullscreen Donald Trump stands with Xi Jinping after arriving at Shenzhen Bao’an airport in China. Photograph: Mandel Ngan/AFP/Getty Images Share 3h ago 04.26 EST As a reminder, Ukraine carried out a major strike on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia, destroying its central road section in an operation involving two strikes over consecutive days.
 The attack earlier this week dealt a significant blow to a key transport link and a symbolic project for Vladimir Putin , as the Russian president sat down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping for talks at the Apec summit.
 My colleague Jakub Krupa has the latest on the Ukraine conflict over on our Europe live blog here:
 Germany hits out after US criticises Ukraine’s deep strikes into Russia – Europe live Read more Share 3h ago 04.11 EST Trump welcomed by Xi as he arrives for summit
 View image in fullscreen US president Donald Trump arrives at Shenzhen airport in China to attend the Apec summit. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters View image in fullscreen Chinese president Xi Jinping welcomes Trump. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters View image in fullscreen Trump salutes next to Xi as they pose for photos. Photograph: Carlos Barría/Reuters Share Updated at  04.12 EST 4h ago 03.57 EST Carney challenges Putin's claim that sanctions no longer work
 While we await Trump to disembark Air Force Once, we have this report from our China correspondent Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen:
 Canada’s Mark Carney has hit back at Vladimir Putin’s earlier assertion that sanctions no longer work in this day and age.
 “Mr Putin can ask his financial institutions, he can ask his oligarch friends, he can ask his hockey players whether or not sanctions are a thing of the past. I think he’ll find out that they’re very real, they’re biting,” Carney told reporters.
 In his address to the summit this morning, Putin had said that “the traditional tools of economic dominance and de facto coercion have largely run their course, having ⁠lost much of their intimidating power”. 
 Speaking at an outdoor press conference as purple clouds lingered ominously in the background, Carney said: “Not for the first time, Vladimir Putin is lying about the situation on the ground. Sanctions are very real and they’re going to continue to increase as long as this war goes on.” 
 View image in fullscreen Canadian prime minister Mark Carney speaks at a press conference on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: Florence Lo/Reuters Carney had previously said he would not boycott a group photo with Putin out of respect for hosts China . But he said if he were to find himself next to the Russian president, he would make Canada’s position clear.
 Carney met China’s president Xi Jinping on Tuesday, with the two countries announcing remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
 The two men also discussed AI, Carney said Wednesday, adding he had taken the opportunity to share Canada’s views on a model for global governance.
 “The absence of any global governance around AI is an enormous risk,” he said. “It’s an enormous economic risk but it’s a biohazard risk, and it’s a risk to democracy, human dignity, other factors... So it is past time to develop global governance frameworks for these sectors.”
 Carney is due to meet Donald Trump later today, he said, where they would discuss efforts to reach a trade deal.
 “We have been making progress... Two steps forward, one step back type thing,” he said.
 He said he fully respected Trump’s engagement with China.
 “I’m going to say something positive here about the initiative around denuclearization, the trilateral meeting that is going to happen,” he said. “Guess what? Canada’s in favor of denuclearization. If the relationship can be used towards that end, we’re very much supportive of it.”
 Share Updated at  03.58 EST 4h ago 03.44 EST Trump arrives in Shenzhen for Apec summit, Chinese state media reports
 Donald Trump has arrived in Shenzhen, China, for the Apec summit, Chinese state media reported.
 We will bring you more as we get it.
